## Saturation adjustment at fixed internal energy and volume (`uv-solver`) {#sec-ch04-equilibrate-uv}

### Summary

A dynamical model knows each cell's density and internal energy, not its temperature. This solver finds the
temperature and the gas-condensate split together, so that the conditions of @sec-ch04-conditions hold and the
internal energy per volume is unchanged: latent heat released by condensation warms the cell. It runs through
`ThermoY` in molar concentrations. Two methods are available. The general method uses the same active-set
least-squares step as the fixed-temperature solver. The partition method is a shortcut for reaction sets in which
every reaction has exactly one vapour and one condensate and no species appears in two reactions.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Satisfy @eq-ch04-conditions-saturation at fixed internal energy and volume.

**Data.** Concentrations and internal energy per volume in; temperature and concentrations out.

**Placement.** `ThermoY` forward, per cell, on CPU or CUDA.

**Activation.** YAML `dynamics: equation-of-state: uv-solver:` `auto` (default), `kkt` or `partition`.

**Guarantee / limits.** `partition` is refused for reaction sets that do not qualify.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

### Numerical method

The method is chosen in `ThermoYImpl::forward` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::forward >}}):

1. A reaction set qualifies for the partition method when every reaction has exactly one vapour consumed and one
   condensate produced, and no species appears in more than one reaction. The check is in `ThermoYImpl::reset`
   ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::reset >}}).
2. `uv-solver: partition` on a set that does not qualify raises an error: "UV partition solver requires disjoint
   vapor-cloud reactions".
3. `uv-solver: auto` passes the choice to the per-cell solver when the set qualifies, and uses the general method
   otherwise. `kkt` always uses the general method.
